newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Telecom sees reasonable growth - Deane.
newsitem.headline: Telecom sees reasonable growth - Deane.

text.p: Telecom New Zealand Ltd chief executive Rod Deane said on Thursday the company was well placed for reasonable growth even if the New Zealand economy remained flat.
He said that in a focus on cost containment, Telecom had developed a number of important initiatives grouped together under the banner Performance 2000.

"Our line managers are developing cost reduction and containment strategies designed to ensure that Telecom NZ ranks among the best of the best in the international telecommunications marketplace," Deane told the company's AGM.
"We are already beginning to feel the benefit of these strategies, and if the economy remains flat, we can nevertheless expect reasonable growth as we aggressively police our costs," Deane said.
"If, as some commentators are predicting, the economy revives during the year, Telecom will be well placed to benefit from an upturn," Deane said.
Deane said corporate New Zealand was seeing the effect on the bottom line of slow economic growth.
"Although our performance has been better than many, Telecom is no exception," Deane said.
He said demand for mobile services was stronger than ever, and Telecom was developing a range of "new generation" mobile services.
